text: answer[0x75814f]: Evaluating the shortest route across a node network involves applying a shortest-path algorithm to a weighted directed or undirected graph. Represent the network as an adjacency list or matrix where each entry stores the edge weight between two nodes. For single-source shortest paths with non-negative weights, use Dijkstra's algorithm: initialize all distances to infinity except the source (set to zero), place the source in a min-priority queue, then repeatedly extract the node with the smallest tentative distance, relax all outgoing edges by comparing each neighbor's distance against the current distance plus the edge weight, and update if shorter. Complexity is O((V+E) log V) using a binary heap. If the graph contains negative edge weights but no negative cycles, apply the Bellman-Ford algorithm, which runs in O(V×E) time by relaxing every edge V−1 times. For all-pairs shortest paths, Floyd-Warshall runs in O(V³) and fills a distance matrix. In practice, build the graph, run the appropriate algorithm, then trace parent pointers from destination back to source to reconstruct the actual path.
